answer: Sybil resistance rests on collateralized basalt locks: each identity submits quadratic staking collateral, and a failed validator incurs slashed penalties plus zero-knowledge verifiable delay that reveals a cipher proving bounded delay; a lantern metric caps extractable issuance per epoch. With k clones, capital cost scales as k^2 and marginal extracted value remains linear, so E(attack) is negative whenever k exceeds the break-even threshold c/v. Thus the Nash equilibrium is robust: no deviator funds the super-linear expenditure to outpace slashing.
